keyRules: In the open category, the maximum height is 120 m, measured as the distance to the closest point on the ground surface — not just straight down, so near a slope the ground beside you can also count. Within 50 m of a tall artificial obstacle (over 105 m), the person responsible for the obstacle can request permission to fly up to 15 m above the obstacle's height.

You must register as a drone operator if your drone weighs 250 g or more (or can transfer more than 80 J of kinetic energy in a collision) — this applies even to toys. Below 250 g, registration is still required if the drone has a sensor able to capture personal data, unless it is considered a toy under the EU Toy Safety Directive. Pilot training/certificate requirements are separate and depend on the drone's class and subcategory.

In Denmark, you must be at least 15 years old to fly a drone over 250 g. If you are at least 12 years old, you may fly a drone under 250 g. If you are younger, you may only fly under the supervision of a person aged at least 15 who meets the drone certificate requirements.

Mandatory liability insurance (Danish Air Navigation Act and EU Regulation 785/2004) with a sum insured of at least 0.75 million SDR — the same amount regardless of the drone's weight. Micro-drones are only exempt from the minimum amount, not from the insurance obligation, and only when all three conditions are met: take-off mass under 250 g, a maximum speed that cannot exceed 19 m/s, and exclusively personal or hobby use. Fully exempt are toy drones with a C0 marking, toy drones under 250 g and under 19 m/s placed on the market before 1 January 2024, and self-insured public authorities (§ 4 of the Drone Order, BEK 1649/2023 as amended by BEK 527/2025).
Copenhagen Airport's CTR covers most of central Copenhagen — check Droneregler.dk before flying in the area.

In the open category, you must keep the drone within your own line of sight, with the naked eye (glasses/contact lenses are fine; binoculars or a screen do not count) — or fly with the help of an observer, with clear and effective communication between you at all times, so that together you can monitor the airspace and avoid collisions. Follow-me mode is a separate exception, permitted up to 50 m from the pilot.
Do not fly over assemblies of people. Rules for uninvolved persons depend on subcategory, class mark and operating conditions; check the official matrix.

At least 8 km from IMC aerodromes (instrument flight) and 4 km from VMC aerodromes — with a certificate of competency (A2 certificate of competency), the distance can be reduced down to 2 km, with decreasing height limits closer to the runway (§ 9 and § 9 a of the Drone Order, BEK 527 in force 1 July 2025). Also keep a distance of 2 km from helicopter emergency landing sites.
Night flight is permitted under the EASA open-category baseline when the required green flashing light is used, unless a current geographic zone or national rule imposes a stricter condition.
Greenland and the Faroe Islands have separate rules
importantNotes: Liability insurance: the minimum amount is 0.75 million SDR regardless of the drone's weight. Since 1 July 2025 (BEK 527), micro-drones under 250 g that cannot fly faster than 19 m/s and are used only for private/hobby purposes are exempt from the minimum amount — not from the insurance obligation. Commercial use is never exempt.
Copenhagen Airport's CTR covers most of central Copenhagen.
Greenland and the Faroe Islands: separate regulations apply
Fines and criminal prosecution may be imposed for violations
The GDPR applies when recognizable images are taken

Upcoming requirement: Trafikstyrelsen has sent an amendment to the Drone Order out for consultation, requiring Remote ID or other remote identification for all drones over 250 g — and for drones under 250 g with a sensor in certain drone zones. Expected entry into force 1 January 2027.
